model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; normalised earnings after capital retention, net debt zero; residual-income on tangible book cross-check)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total net revenue (net interest income + non-interest income, net of interest expense). 1H26 actual 31,081 (Q1 15,231, Q2 15,850 incl. Brex from 7 Apr 2026; SEC XBRL Revenues / InterestIncomeExpenseNet 24,519 + NoninterestIncome 6,562) plus 2H26 at ~16,200/qtr on seasonal Q3/Q4 purchase-volume strength and a full quarter of Brex. FY2025 statutory 53,434 contains only 7.5 months of Discover and is not a usable base. FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027; the remaining Q4 2026 flow (~$3bn FCFE) is not separately credited, which roughly offsets discounting FY2027 one year instead of ~1.26.
inputs.share_count_basis: 613.5m common shares outstanding per the Q2 2026 10-Q cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~3m dilutive RSU/PSU (Q2 2026 weighted diluted 621.1m was struck before the Q2 buyback cadence). Includes the ~10.6m shares issued for Brex (Apr 2026) and the ~255m issued for Discover (May 2025). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and buybacks (FY2025 $4,099m, 1H26 $5,540m) are simply the distribution channel for the FCFE and the excess capital credited in the equity bridge -- reducing the count as well would double-count.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is ZERO by construction. Capital One is a bank holding company: deposits ($484.3bn at 30 Jun 2026) and senior/sub debt and securitisations ($44.7bn) are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash and restricted cash ($55.9bn) is liquidity held against that funding, not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E normalised FCFE (pre-preferred) = normalised NPAT ~11,940 (63,500 x pre-tax 23.8% x (1 - 21%)) less capital retained ~2,450 to hold tangible common equity in line with 4.5% balance-sheet growth (0.855 x g x revenue; required TCE ~$54.4bn = TBV $60.4bn less ~$6bn estimated excess). Normalisation of 1H26 GAAP NI 5,194: + Discover/Brex integration expense (~$600m pre-tax 1H, ~$298m in Q2 per the Q2 call) + acquired-intangible amortisation ($999m pre-tax 1H, non-cash, and the intangibles are already excluded from tangible book) - the $664m Q2 reserve release and a growth-build (provision normalised to net charge-offs ~$7.5bn 1H + ~$0.45bn build), all at a 22% tax rate -> ~5,820 1H / ~11,650 annualised, vs the engine's FY0 11,940 (includes 2H seasonal revenue). Q2 2025 GAAP loss of -4,277 (Day-1 CECL build on acquired non-PCD Discover loans + merger costs) is excluded as one-off acquisition accounting.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory OCF less capex (FY2025 26,140; 1H26 13,547) is inflated by the non-cash provision add-back and loan-sale/trading movements and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank. reported_fcf here is the normalised FCFE proxy BEFORE the SBC charge, so last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash flow statement add-back): FY2024 $569m, FY2025 $776m (includes Discover replacement awards), 1H26 $346m -> ~$700m FY2026E run-rate, ~1.1% of revenue. Net-share-settlement withholding taxes are not separately material in the XBRL facts.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added in the bridge (matching-asset rule satisfied the other way).
inputs.buyback_note: 1H26 repurchases $5,540m (Q1 $2,793m, Q2 $2,747m) under the $16bn authorisation, after FY2025 $4,099m (mostly 2H25 post-close). The pace (~$11bn annualised) exceeds normalised FCFE (~$9.5bn), i.e. COF is running down the post-Discover CET1 surplus -- consistent with the excess-capital line in the equity bridge.
inputs.book_value_anchor: 30 Jun 2026: stockholders' equity $113,793m - preferred $5,407m (PreferredStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapitalNetOfDiscount; 4.98m shares) - goodwill $31,866m - other intangibles $16,077m = tangible common equity $60,443m = ~$98.0/share on 616.5m. Price $200.2 = 2.04x TBV. TCE is net of AOCI -$6,300m (mostly AFS securities marks) which accretes back as the book pulls to par -- an unmodelled upside of up to ~$10/share. FY2024 TBV was ~$40.6bn on 383.6m (~$106/share): the all-stock Discover purchase at a premium to TBV plus the ~$8.8bn Day-1 CECL double-count REDUCED tangible book per share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.25 x US ERP 5.0% = 10.45%, rounded to 10.5%. Beta 1.25 reflects a subprime-skewed card lender (COF's 5-year observed beta ~1.2-1.4) -- above the 1.0 used for NAB.AX. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, integration and CFPB risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial (operating lease ROU assets ~$1.5bn vs $114bn equity); lease cost sits inside non-interest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock is a senior claim: deducted at its $5,407m carrying value in the equity bridge (conservative vs capitalising ~$230-260m/yr dividends at 10.5%), and the flows are pre-preferred.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine exactly as NAB.AX (2026-09-24): SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with capital retention = g x required tangible equity is the clean-surplus equivalent and runs through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. Engine mapping: revenue = total net revenue; ebitda_margin_path = normalised pre-tax profit (revenue - non-interest expense ex integration costs and ex acquired-intangible amortisation - through-cycle provision) PLUS SBC, as % of revenue; FY2026E 24.9% = 100 - adj. efficiency 51.5% - provision 24.7% + SBC 1.1%; sbc_pct_path 1.1%; da_pct 0 (bank D&A is inside opex; acquired-intangible amortisation is excluded as non-cash and already out of tangible book); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to grow tangible common equity with the balance sheet = 0.855 x g (required TCE $54.4bn / revenue $63.5bn); cash_tax_rate_path = 21% (1H26 effective 20.2%; FY2024 19.7%); wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0. Equity bridge: + estimated excess CET1 capital, - preferred at carrying value. ONE-OFFS EXCLUDED: Q2 2025 Day-1 CECL build and merger costs (GAAP loss -$4,277m); Discover/Brex integration expense (~$1.2bn/yr through 2H 2027, treated as a transition cost; the bear case charges it); Q2 2026 $664m reserve release. RESIDUAL-INCOME CROSS-CHECK on tangible book: normalised FY26E NPAT 11,940 (pre-preferred) on REQUIRED tangible equity $54.4bn = ROTE ~22% (19.3% on the full $60.4bn TBV incl. the surplus); steady-state P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (22 - 3)/(10.5 - 3) = 2.53x x $54.4bn = $137.8bn, + $6.0bn excess - $5.4bn preferred = $138.4bn = ~$224/share. The engine base ($241) sits ~$17 above because FY27-31 grow 4-5% (above the 3% terminal) at a ~22% incremental ROTE. Equivalently the base is ~12.4x normalised FY27 EPS to common (~$19.5, below the ~$21.5 street forward EPS implied by a 9.3x forward P/E). Base = 2.46x TBV vs 2.04x at the market price. MEMORY: first valuation of COF; no prior model. DATA: no filing text is extracted for COF (XBRL-only ticker); bank lines (provision, non-interest expense, goodwill, intangibles, preferred, AOCI, deposits) were read from SEC companyfacts (CIK 927628) for this build. CET1 ratio and RWA are NOT in XBRL -- the excess-capital line is an ESTIMATE; refresh from the Q3 2026 earnings supplement (due ~late Oct 2026).

equity_bridge.item: Estimated excess CET1 capital above an ~11.5-12% operating target
equity_bridge.note: ESTIMATE, not a filed number: CET1 ratio and RWA are not in XBRL. Post-Discover CET1 ran ~14% in 2H25; 1H26 buybacks ($5.5bn) and the Brex cash consideration (~$2.75bn, ~40bp CET1) have consumed part of it. ~1.2pp x ~$500bn RWA = ~$6bn. The $11bn/yr buyback pace is the observable evidence. Refresh from the Q3 2026 supplement.
PreferredStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapitalNetOfDiscount, 30 Jun 2026 10-Q; 4,980,700 shares. Senior to common; flows are pre-preferred-dividend.

historical_growth.tbv_per_share_fy24_to_q2_26: ~$106 -> ~$98 (down: stock issued for Discover above TBV, Day-1 CECL double-count)
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-path average. Every statutory CAGR is distorted by the May 2025 all-stock Discover acquisition (revenue and equity step-ups, FY2025 EPS 4.03 depressed by the Q2 2025 Day-1 CECL loss). Pre-deal organic revenue grew 8.7%/yr FY21-24 in a period of card-balance rebuilding and rising rates; forward balance-sheet growth of 4-5% is more representative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (29.3% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (16.0%) and EPS (-39.2%): all three are acquisition artefacts, not organic trends. Free-cash-flow CAGRs are not meaningful for a bank (OCF includes provision add-backs and loan-sale flows) and are left null.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR is not computed: owner-FCF is not the model for a bank. SBC grew $513m (FY23) -> $776m (FY25) largely from Discover replacement awards, roughly in line with revenue.

base.growth_rationale: Total net revenue. FY27 5.0%: a full year of Brex (+~0.8pp), Discover network revenue as the credit back-book migrates off Visa through Q1 2027, and ~4% card-loan growth, partly offset by Fed easing compressing card yields. Tapers to 3.0% (US nominal GDP ~4% less modest share/yield drift).
base.margin_rationale: Normalised pre-tax profit + SBC on revenue. FY27 24.4% = 100 - efficiency 51.0% - provision 25.7% + SBC 1.1%: roughly half the remaining ~$1.2bn of the $2.5bn synergies land (the other half reinvested in network/Brex growth and competed away), while provisioning rises from 1H26's ~24.7% to a through-cycle 25.7% as reserve releases stop and NCOs drift off the 4.71% card rate. FY28+ 25.0% = 100 - 50.6 - 25.5 + 1.1 at full synergy run-rate. Pre-deal FY2019 ran ~25.6% on the same basis (24.8% pre-tax + 0.8% SBC), so the base gives the enlarged company no margin credit for the owned network beyond the synergies already guided.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to grow tangible common equity with the balance sheet = 0.855 x g (required TCE $54.4bn / FY26E revenue $63.5bn). At 5% growth 4.3% of revenue (~$2.9bn, ~24% of NPAT retained, ~76% distributed); at 3% terminal 2.6% (~14% retained). Implied incremental ROTE ~19-20%, in line with the normalised FY26E ROTE.

bull.growth_rationale: Discover network takes a growing share of COF's own card and debit volume plus third-party issuers; Brex compounds in commercial card; card-loan growth ~5-6%. Terminal 3.5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Full $2.7bn synergy upside retained plus network economics beyond the deal model: efficiency 50.3% -> 49.0%, provision 25.2% -> 24.8% (benign unemployment, NCOs near 4.5% card), + SBC 1.1%.

bear.growth_rationale: US recession in FY27: card balances shrink in real terms, fee income falls with purchase volume, rate cuts compress yields; network migration friction (narrower international acceptance) costs premium/travel accounts. Terminal 2.0%.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27 10.6% = 100 - efficiency 52.5% (synergies delayed, integration costs charged) - provision 38.0% (card NCOs ~7%, CECL reserve build) + 1.1%; comparable to FY2020 (GAAP NI 9.5% of revenue). FY28 17.1% as reserves peak and NCOs ease. Mature 22.1% = 100 - 52.0 - 27.0 + 1.1: through-cycle credit is permanently worse on the enlarged subprime book and part of the synergy is competed/regulated away (CFPB 360 Savings restitution, interchange/APR caps).
bear.capex_rationale: 0.855 x g, as base; low retention in FY27-28 because the balance sheet barely grows, and the excess capital in the bridge absorbs the recession.

scenario_narratives.base: The Discover integration completes on schedule (back-book converted by Q1 2027, $2.5bn run-rate synergies by 2H 2027) but roughly half the benefit is reinvested or competed away. Credit normalises to through-cycle levels rather than staying at the 1H26 reserve-release run-rate. Normalised ROTE ~19-20% on ~$60bn of tangible equity, 3-5% balance-sheet growth, ~76-86% of earnings returned via dividends and buybacks. Value lands at ~2.5x tangible book vs the market's 2.0x: the market is discounting either through-cycle credit worse than this base, synergies below the guided run-rate, or a cost of equity nearer 12%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Owning the Discover/PULSE rails proves to be the Amex-style structural advantage the deal was sold on: COF's own volume migrates, network and interchange economics stay in-house, Brex compounds commercial card, and credit stays benign. Efficiency falls to ~49% and ROTE settles in the low-to-mid 20s.
scenario_narratives.bear: A US recession arrives while two integrations are live. Card NCOs rise to ~7% on a book with roughly double its nearest competitor's subprime share, CECL front-loads the reserve build (FY27 earnings fall ~55%), synergies slip and the CFPB 360 Savings case settles expensively. Through-cycle ROTE resets to the mid-teens. The excess capital cushions the downturn without a raise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: ~75% of revenue is unsecured consumer card lending skewed to subprime/near-prime, charge-offs are late-cycle and the 1H26 earnings benefit from a reserve release; two integrations run concurrently and management still declines to guide an efficiency ratio; the CFPB 360 Savings litigation (>$2bn alleged) is unresolved. Bull cut to 25%: it requires network economics beyond the guided synergies and a benign credit cycle for a decade.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is negative because the price sits BELOW both the house (SBC-expensed) and street (SBC-as-non-cash) weighted values; it is not located between them.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capital One is valued as a bank: normalised free cash flow to equity (earnings after the capital needed to grow the balance sheet) capitalised at a 10.5% cost of equity, with deposits and debt treated as operating funding (net debt zero), preferred deducted, and an estimated CET1 surplus credited. The base year is a normalised FY2026E that strips the Discover Day-1 CECL loss, integration costs, acquired-intangible amortisation and the Q2 2026 reserve release, and charges a through-cycle provision. A residual-income check on ~$98 of tangible book per share (P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g)) is recorded in inputs.notes. Multiples sanity check (2026-09-26): the P/E trip (89.9x) is an artefact of FY2025 EPS depressed by the Day-1 Discover CECL build and a part-year of Discover; on TTM (15.4x) and normalised FY26E (12.5x) EPS the value is below the 20.3x 10-year average, so no driver was changed. See sanity_check_banner.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 1pp of revenue in provisions is ~$500m of after-tax earnings (~$0.8/share per year); the base assumes through-cycle, not current, charge-offs.
The excess-capital line ($6bn, ~$10/share) is an estimate -- CET1 and RWA are not in XBRL.
Synergy realisation and network migration: base credits only ~half of the remaining guided synergies.
CFPB 360 Savings litigation (>$2bn alleged withheld interest) is charged only in the bear case.
AOCI of -$6.3bn depresses tangible book and will partly accrete back -- unmodelled upside.
Cost of equity: at 2.0x TBV the value is sensitive to CoE; each 1pp is worth roughly 12-15%.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_banner: Sanity check tripped on P/E only: the model's weighted value implies 89.9x FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS ($2.63) against a 10-year average of 20.3x. That is a denominator artefact, not an over-rich model. FY2025 GAAP net income ($2,453m, EPS $4.03) contains the Q2 2025 GAAP loss of -$4,277m, which is the Day-1 CECL reserve build on acquired non-PCD Discover loans plus merger costs, both one-off acquisition accounting. It also contains only ~7.5 months of Discover earnings while the share count already includes the ~255m shares issued for the deal. The model never uses FY2025 as its base: it capitalises a normalised FY2026E FCFE (priority-1 normalisation is already built in), so no driver was changed. Against honest denominators the same value is 15.4x trailing-twelve-month SBC-adjusted EPS to Q2 2026 (~$15.35; the market price is 13.0x) and 12.5x normalised FY2026E EPS to common (~$18.96; market 10.6x), both below the 20.3x average and well inside the 40.6x trip line. The other rules pass. P/B of 1.33x sits at the top of the 10-year range (avg 0.93x, max 1.33x in FY2025) because the all-stock Discover purchase added ~$48bn of goodwill and intangibles to book; on tangible book the value is ~2.4x against ~2.0x at market. P/Sales of 2.82x is also at the top of its range (avg 1.72x, max 2.84x) and is consistent with a ~25% normalised pre-tax margin. The fixes on the priority list were rejected as indefensible. Passing the P/E rule on FY2025 EPS would need a value below ~$107, about 1.2x required tangible equity, which implies a cost of equity near 19% for a ~22% ROTE bank. A regulatory WACC premium would double-count the CFPB/interchange risk already charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight. The through-cycle revenue CAGR (8.7% organic, 13.4% statutory) sits above the 3-5% growth path, so a growth cap does not bind. EV/EBITDA exit caps do not apply to a bank. Framing: a normalised ~20% ROTE card franchise returning ~75-85% of earnings, bought for income plus modest compounding, not a multi-bagger. The risk is credit-cycle and integration execution, which the 25% bear weight carries.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 174.24-259.64.
data_sources.financials: COF_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, through Q2 2026) plus SEC companyfacts API (CIK 927628) for provision, non-interest expense, goodwill, intangibles, preferred, AOCI, deposits, buybacks, dividends and the 10-Q cover share count.
data_sources.qualitative: COF_Analysis.json (2026-09-26): Q2 2026 call (21 Jul 2026) -- $664m reserve release, ~$298m integration expense, NCO 4.71%, synergies $2.5-2.7bn by 2H 2027, Brex closed 7 Apr 2026.
